permutationLabel: Injecting drug use, previous MRSA, SIRS, groin site
summary: 34-year-old man who injects drugs: 3 days of a painful swelling in the right groin at an injection site, previous MRSA abscess; T 38.4 °C, HR 104; 5 cm fluctuant swelling with cellulitis.

inputs.hpi: Injects heroin into the right groin. Three days of a painful swelling at the injection site with fevers. MRSA abscess on the arm drained last year. No bleeding from the site.

exam.skin: Right groin over the femoral triangle: 5 cm tender fluctuant swelling with 4 cm of surrounding erythema, multiple injection marks. No expansile pulsation felt but femoral pulse close by. Distal pulses present.

surgicalHistory: Incision and drainage of left arm abscess (MRSA)
inputs.socialHistory: Injects heroin into the groin. Unstable housing.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Cutaneous abscess of groin (MRSA risk)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Groin injection-site abscess with surrounding cellulitis and SIRS in a person who injects drugs, previous MRSA. Exclude femoral pseudoaneurysm before drainage.

mustNotMiss.note: A groin "abscess" at an injection site can be an infected femoral pseudoaneurysm; incising it causes catastrophic haemorrhage. Duplex before drainage. Vascular surgical practice with no guideline statement cited here, so quality until the surgeon decides the severity.
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: No engine has infected femoral pseudoaneurysm; PANE top 3: Acute appendicitis, Skin abscess, Acute cholecystitis (the Groin site chip adds groin_swelling).

mustInclude.note: Imaging of the femoral vessels before incising a groin injection-site swelling. No guideline statement cited; quality until the surgeon decides the severity.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: No engine recommends imaging a groin injection-site swelling before incision.
No blood-borne virus screen suggested for a person who injects drugs.

guideline.name: IDSA practice guideline — diagnosis and management of skin and soft tissue infections (2014 update)
guideline.section: Purulent SSTI (abscess): incision and drainage; antibiotics active against MRSA when SIRS, immunocompromise or failed drainage; culture of abscess material. Non-purulent cellulitis: agent active against streptococci; severe: IV antibiotics and assess for necrotising infection. Necrotising infections: prompt surgical consultation, vancomycin plus piperacillin-tazobactam (or carbapenem), clindamycin for toxin suppression in streptococcal NF
guideline.citation: Stevens DL, Bisno AL, Chambers HF, et al. Practice guidelines for the diagnosis and management of skin and soft tissue infections: 2014 update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America. Clin Infect Dis. 2014;59:e10–52.

rationale: Permutation: MRSA risk, SIRS and a groin injection site. IDSA 2014 adds MRSA-active antibiotics with SIRS. The groin site adds a must-not-miss (infected pseudoaneurysm) that should be imaged before any incision.
